name: Northern Pame
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.

catalog_quote: Northern Pame has two contrastive tones, which are a high tone and a rising tone. Tone is contrastive on the lexical root, which is also the location of stress. [...] Thus, identical to other Pame descriptions (Avelino 1997, 2002, Gibson and Bartholomew 1979, Gibson 1956 and Manrique 1967) the present research describes tone as fundamentally a pitch-accent system. There are a number of factors that should be kept in mind with Northern Pame tone. First, as mentioned previously tone is only contrastive on the lexical (and stressed) root, which with one exception, is always monosyllabic. Pitch variations on non-root syllables can always be determined by the pitch of the root syllable. [p.33] ... In summary, Northern Pame tones must be either high or rising and are contrastive only on the stressed syllable. [p.36] || Avelino 1997:156: Es necesario aclarar que el acento no es distintivo, y es predecible: en una palabra, la unidad de mayor intensidad se encuentra en la sílaba de la raíz; esta descripción permite afirmar que tanto el acento, como el tono tienen un anclaje morfológico, ambos ponen en prominencia al elemento en que coinciden: la raíz.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is predictable and non-contrastive: it falls on the (normally monosyllabic) lexical root syllable; prefixes/proclitic person-number markers are pretonic and suffixes (dual/plural etc.) and the second vowel of VhV/VʔV roots are post-tonic. The two lexical/grammatical tones (high vs rising) contrast only on that stressed root syllable; pitch elsewhere is derived from the root tone. Avelino 1997:156 states the same independently: 'el acento no es distintivo, y es predecible: en una palabra, la unidad de mayor intensidad se encuentra en la sílaba de la raíz'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either source.
new_statements.exceptions: Berthiaume notes one root that is polysyllabic ('with one exception'); rising tone spreads rightward over post-tonic syllables instead of lengthening when the root/stem is polysyllabic or has a sonorant coda (p.35). Avelino: stress has no demarcative function (fn., p.156).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement (root within the morphological word, citation/possessed forms such as prefix+root+suffix nouns and inflected verbs). Language is a restricted-tone / pitch accent system: two tones (Berthiaume) or three (Avelino 1997, 2002) contrastive only on the stressed root syllable; stress itself identified by intensity (Avelino's CECIL intensity traces) and by being the tone-bearing, non-neutralising position.
new_statements.identity_note: Both primary sources describe Northern Pame (Xi'iuy of the Cuesta Blanca / Ciudad del Maíz-Alaquines area, San Luis Potosí) = nort2984. Berthiaume 2012 also reviews Gibson 1956 (Central Pame, Santa María Acapulco = cent2145) and Manrique 1967 (Jiliapan = Southern Pame), which report the same root-stress + tone-on-stressed-syllable pattern but are different languages; those were not used for the statement.

tone_statements.citation: Avelino, Heriberto. 1998. Epéntesis y organización prosódica en pame norte. Dimensión Antropológica año 5, vol. 13 (mayo-agosto 1998): 129-150. México: INAH.
tone_statements.quote: La representación de vocales rearticuladas V’V corresponde en realidad a vocales con un tono descendente, este tono se “reparte” en toda la palabra y la parte final se propaga al sufijo. La alternancia en los ejemplos entre raíces con vocal rearticulada y simple sigue la transcripción alofónica que aquí mantengo. El análisis de los procesos tonales está en el libro más reciente en Heriberto Avelino (en prensa).
tone_statements.translation: The representation of rearticulated vowels V'V in reality corresponds to vowels with a falling tone; this tone is 'distributed' over the whole word and its final part spreads onto the suffix. The alternation in the examples between roots with a rearticulated vowel and a simple vowel follows the allophonic transcription I keep here. The analysis of the tonal processes is in the most recent book, Heriberto Avelino (in press).

tone_statements.summary: Falling (descending) tone realised over root V'V and spread to suffix; full tonal analysis deferred to Avelino 2002.

sources.note: The article is about vowel/consonant epenthesis under dual/plural number suffixation and syllable structure (Itô-style prosodic licensing), not tone; tone appears only in a footnote stating that the 'rearticulated' V'V vowels of roots are in reality vowels bearing a falling tone which is distributed over the whole word with its final portion spreading onto the suffix, and that the analysis of tonal processes is given in Avelino (en prensa) [= the known 2002 'Sandhi tonal en pame norte'].
